The test is suppressed while the hard circuit faults P0C44 or P0C45 are active, so P0C46 usually means a signal that is present but noisy. Loose terminals, contact corrosion or a harness that moves with the battery are the usual causes; wiggling the wiring with live data running helps locate it. Sensor B uses P0CD9.

causes.label: Loose or spread terminal at the coolant sensor connector
Corrosion at connector or ground point
Harness rubbing or cracked near the battery coolant lines

symptoms: MIL that may go out again for a while
Jumping coolant temperature in live data

P0C47.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P0C47.description: P0C47 means the controller sees an electrical fault on the line that commands battery coolant pump A. GM's 2019 tables catch open, short to ground and short to power by current: with the pump on, less than 200 mA or more than 3 A on the control line count as failures, with the pump off less than 120 µA; 4 s within 5 s set a Type B code. Porsche reports P0C4700 on the 2015–2017 Cayenne plug-in hybrid (92A), often with the MIL as the only symptom, and blames corroded ground pin 6B, a corroded pump connector or poor wiring. Audi links it on the 2024 Q4 e-tron to corrosion at splice J1 with reduced power. Bentley warns that on 2025–2026 Continental GT and Flying Spur hybrids it can keep the car from switching to ready mode. P0C48 and P0C49 are the low and high variants.

causes.label: Corroded or painted ground point or corroded pump connector (Porsche Cayenne 92A)
Corroded splice or chafed harness in the pump circuit (Audi Q4 e-tron, Bentley)
Failed electric coolant pump or its relay

symptoms: MIL, frequently the only sign
Electrical or drive system warning with reduced power
Vehicle refuses to become ready to drive

P0C48.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Control Circuit Low
P0C48.description: P0C48 narrows a fault on the control line of battery coolant pump A down to a signal that stays too low, as caused by a short to ground or a driver output that cannot pull the line up. Ford lists the code for the 2020 Explorer, Police Interceptor Utility and Lincoln Aviator with the hybrid powertrain. Bulletins 20-2293 and 20-2345 group it with P0C49, P0C4A, P0C4B, P0CFF, P2B29 and other pump and battery codes that light the MIL and are stored in the PCM; the cause is the software of the battery energy control module, which is reprogrammed. Other makers, GM for instance, cover the same failure inside the broader code P0C47. CARB requires output components of battery thermal management to be checked for circuit faults. If the pump really stops, battery power is limited.

causes.label: Battery control module software (Ford/Lincoln 2020 hybrids, TSB 20-2345)
Pump control wire shorted to ground
Internal fault in the pump electronics pulling the line low

symptoms: MIL on
Hybrid system message, battery power possibly limited

P0C49.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Control Circuit High
P0C49.description: P0C49 is set when the control signal to battery coolant pump A remains too high, for example because the line is shorted to battery voltage or, on a pulled-up input, interrupted. Ford uses it on the 2020 Explorer, Police Interceptor Utility and Lincoln Aviator hybrids. Bulletins 20-2293 and 20-2345 list it right after P0C48 among a group of MIL codes for the battery and electronics coolant pumps; Ford traces them to the battery energy control module software and fixes them by reprogramming. GM, by contrast, folds short to power into P0C47. CARB requires the outputs of battery thermal management to be monitored for circuit faults. If the pump actually loses its command, the battery heats up faster under load and the system reduces power. P0C48 is the low counterpart, P0C4D concerns the supply voltage instead.

causes.label: Battery control module software (Ford/Lincoln 2020 hybrids, TSB 20-2293/20-2345)
Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Control line interrupted at the pump connector

symptoms: MIL on
Battery power reduced during long climbs or fast charging

P0C4A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Control Performance
P0C4A.description: P0C4A says pump A runs electrically but does not achieve its cooling effect. The 2011 Chevrolet Volt fails the test when the pump has been on for over 60 s and the pack inlet coolant temperature has moved by less than 5 °C, rated Type B. GM's bulletin PI0798A (Volt 2011–2015, Ampera 2012, ELR 2014–2016) traces the code after draining and refilling to trapped air, cured by a vacuum purge. Porsche explains for the 2018 Panamera 4 E-Hybrid that the pump reports dry running when its speed rises while current drops, a condition that can need a long stretch of driving before it is logged. Audi (Q4 e-tron 2022) and Bentley (Bentayga and Flying Spur Hybrid, EV speed capped near 48 km/h) also bleed first, Ford reflashes the battery module. FCA's Pacifica Hybrid uses P0C4A for inverter overtemperature instead.

causes.label: Air trapped in the battery coolant loop, often after a coolant service
Low coolant level or a leak in the low-temperature loop
Worn or failing coolant pump
Battery control module software (Ford/Lincoln 2020 hybrids)

symptoms: MIL shortly after cooling system work
Electric drive warning, reduced power or capped EV speed
Gurgling noise from the coolant loop

P0C4B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P0C4B.description: P0C4B refers to the power feed of battery coolant pump A rather than its command line: the controller sees no or only an implausible supply voltage at the pump, typically because a fuse, relay, connector or wire in the feed is open. Ford documents the code on its 2020 hybrids. On the Escape HEV built up to 10 June 2020, bulletin 20-2221 lists P0C4B with other battery codes in the battery energy control module and cures the MIL by reprogramming PCM and BECM; bulletins 20-2293 and 20-2345 name it for the Explorer and Aviator hybrids. Without a software cause, the fuse and relay in the pump feed come first. CARB requires the electrical components of battery thermal management to be monitored. P0C4C and P0C4D are the low and high variants of the same supply.

causes.label: Battery control module software (Ford Escape HEV, Explorer and Aviator 2020)
Blown fuse or failed relay in the pump supply
Open feed wire or pushed-out pin at the pump connector

symptoms: MIL on
Battery coolant pump not running, power limited when warm

P0C4C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P0C4C.description: P0C4C reports that the supply voltage reaching battery coolant pump A is below the expected level while the circuit is not fully open. Typical reasons are high resistance in the feed, a corroded fuse contact, a weak relay, a poor ground or a short to ground that drags the line down. No manufacturer documents P0C4C publicly. Ford uses the sibling P0C4B for the open supply circuit on its 2020 Escape, Explorer and Aviator hybrids, and Bentley's bulletin on P0C4700 for 2025–2026 Continental GT and Flying Spur hybrids shows what such a feed contains: a 10 A fuse, a relay and a harness route that can chafe at the rear suspension. CARB requires the electrical parts of battery thermal management to be monitored. A pump that receives too little voltage runs slowly or not at all.

causes.label: High resistance from corroded fuse, relay contacts or connector
Poor pump ground connection
Supply wire chafed and shorted to ground

symptoms: MIL or hybrid or EV warning
Coolant pump running slowly or intermittently
Battery power reduced when the pack warms up

P0C4D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Coolant Pump A Supply Voltage Circuit High
P0C4D.description: P0C4D is the counterpart to P0C4C: the voltage measured on the supply of battery coolant pump A is higher than the controller allows. That can come from a feed wire shorted to another, more highly loaded circuit, from a relay that stays closed when the pump should be off, or from an overall excessive on-board voltage, for example a faulty DC/DC converter. No manufacturer documents P0C4D publicly. Ford's bulletins for the 2020 Escape, Explorer and Aviator hybrids name the sibling P0C4B for the open supply, and Bentley describes the feed of the same pump with fuse and relay for 2025–2026 hybrids. CARB requires the electrical components of battery thermal management to be monitored. If several modules log overvoltage at once, the 12 V supply is the more likely culprit than the pump circuit.

causes.label: Supply wire shorted to another voltage-carrying circuit
Pump relay sticking closed
Excessive 12 V system voltage from a faulty DC/DC converter

symptoms: MIL or hybrid or EV warning
Coolant pump running although the system is switched off

P0C4E.title: Drive Motor A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P0C4E.description: P0C4E says the resolver offset of drive motor A was learned, yet the learned value is unacceptable. That offset lines up the zero point of the resolver with the rotor magnets. GM rejects a correction angle beyond 30 degrees, or a new value that differs from the stored one by more than 10 degrees; the learn happens at key-off with the motor under 20 rpm and over 192 V on the DC link. Volt and ELR tables rate it Type A, and from 2016 the deviation has to show up on five key-off cycles. Kia links P0C4E00 on 2022-24 Sorento PHEV AWD to a jerky change between electric and hybrid drive and cures it with a new transaxle plus updated hybrid control software (TSB TRA112). P0C17 is the case with no valid learn at all.

causes.label: Resolver or rotor position shifted after replacing the motor, resolver stator or transaxle
Internal transaxle fault on affected Kia Sorento PHEV models (TSB TRA112)
Hybrid or motor control software that needs an update
Damaged resolver that delivers a shifted angle

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, often first noticed after a repair
Jerk or rough feel when switching between electric and hybrid drive
Reduced electric drive power

P0C4F.title: Drive Motor B Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P0C4F.description: P0C4F covers the second traction motor: its resolver offset learn finished, but the angle it produced lies outside what the controller will accept. GM applies the same two tests as for motor A, an absolute correction above 30 degrees or a change of over 10 degrees against the value kept from earlier learns, both checked at key-off with the rotor nearly still and more than 192 V available. The 2011 Volt sets it on one trip as Type A; the 2016 and 2019 Volt tables also say Type A but wait for five key-off cycles with the angle out of range. No bulletin for this code has been published. A large offset jump usually means something mechanical changed, so the check after a motor or sensor job matters most. P0C18 means motor B was never learned.

causes.label: Motor B resolver stator fitted in a different position after a repair
Learn disturbed by a moving rotor or unstable high voltage at key-off
Damaged motor B resolver giving a shifted angle

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after shutdown cycles
Reduced propulsion or motor B unavailable
Unusual noise or shudder under electric drive

P0C50.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit A
P0C50.description: A resolver has two pickup windings set 90 degrees apart, one giving a sine and one a cosine signal. The codes P0C50 onward judge each of those circuits on its own, while P0A3F to P0A43 judge the combined angle signal. GM names the S1/S3 winding Circuit A and the S2/S4 winding Circuit B. P0C50 is the general entry for Circuit A of motor A, used when the controller sees a fault in that line without classing it as a low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM covers the same winding only through P0C52 and P0C53. CARB requires circuit faults of such inputs to be detected and stored separately from out-of-range faults. Expect a warning lamp and possibly lost electric drive.

causes.label: Open wire or loose terminal in the Circuit A (first pickup winding) lines
Corroded or damaged connector between resolver and motor control module
Defective pickup winding inside the resolver stator
Fault in the resolver input stage of the motor control module

symptoms: Hybrid or drive system warning together with the check engine lamp
Electric drive switched off or reduced power
Vehicle may not reach ready mode

P0C51.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit A Range/Performance
P0C51.description: P0C51 means the first resolver winding of motor A (Circuit A) delivers a signal that is electrically present but not believable, for example unsteady or out of step with the second winding. Bentley uses it on 2025 Continental GT, GTC and Flying Spur hybrids, logged by the e-drive control unit at address 0051 next to P0A4000 and later P0C5B00, with a drive system message in the cluster. Bulletin 2080242 asks for logged measured values, a check of the sensor and power electronics plugs for bent pins, weak terminal grip, moisture or corrosion, then basic settings; revision 3 adds a new 90-degree connector. No set threshold is published. P0C52 to P0C54 cover low, high and sporadic faults of the same line.

causes.label: Weak terminal grip or bent pins at the sensor or power electronics connector
Moisture, oil or corrosion in the resolver connectors
Faulty 90-degree connector on the affected Bentley models (TPI 2080242/3)
Resolver winding with degraded output

symptoms: Drive system fault message in the instrument cluster
No electric or hybrid driving mode available
Fault may come and go with temperature or vibration

P0C52.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit A Low
P0C52.description: P0C52 reports that the DC reference level on Circuit A of the motor A resolver, the S1/S3 winding in GM terms, has dropped too low, which points to a short to ground or a line pulled down. GM fails it below 0.5 V on the 2011 Volt, 2012 two-mode trucks, 2013 eAssist and 2016 ELR, and below 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt. Timing ranges from 50 of 80 samples taken every 10.4 ms (one trip, Type A) to 0.525 s within 0.8375 s on the 2016 Volt or 0.25 s within 0.375 s on the 2019 Volt (both Type B). Bentley finds P0C5200, often with P0C5C00, on 2020-22 Bentayga Hybrids with a chafed 12 V transmission harness. Unlike P0A41, which rates the whole signal, this code names one winding.

causes.label: Chafed or pinched transmission harness shorting a Circuit A line to ground (Bentley TPI 2066714)
Water or corrosion in the resolver connector
Shorted S1/S3 winding inside the resolver stator
Faulty resolver input in the motor control module

symptoms: Check engine lamp, often with P0C5C stored at the same time
Electric drive shut off or power reduced
On some hybrids the engine runs constantly or the car will not start

P0C53.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit A High
P0C53.description: P0C53 is the high counterpart of P0C52: the reference level on the S1/S3 winding circuit of the motor A resolver rises above its window, typical of a short to a voltage source or an open line that floats up. GM uses an upper limit of 4.5 V on the 2011 Volt, 2013 eAssist and 2016 Volt and ELR, 4.9 V on the 2019 Volt and only 3.0 V on the 2012 two-mode Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Sierra and Silverado hybrids. It reacts faster than on the low side: 20 of 30 samples (about 208 ms) on the 2011 Volt, 0.2125 s within 0.3125 s on the 2016 Volt. MIL logic is Type A on the 2011 Volt and the 2012 trucks, Type B on eAssist and the later Volt. No bulletin names this code for motor A.

causes.label: Open S1 or S3 line or a terminal that has backed out, letting the input drift high
Circuit A line shorted to a voltage-carrying wire in the harness
Broken S1/S3 winding in the resolver stator
Faulty resolver input in the motor control module

symptoms: Check engine lamp with hybrid system message
Reduced propulsion or electric drive unavailable
Rough engine running on vehicles that use motor A for starting

P0C54.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit A Intermittent/Erratic
P0C54.description: P0C54 stands for short dropouts or jumps on Circuit A of the motor A resolver that never last long enough to count as a steady low or high fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM handles the same situation differently: on its 2013 eAssist cars the resolver circuit checks run a retry scheme that lets the drive recover from brief faults, and only light the MIL through P0C52 or P0C53 once the trouble repeats, either about 5 s of failure within roughly 10 s or 10 s of accumulated failure over 30 minutes. Typical triggers are loose terminals, a cable that moves with the drivetrain or moisture in the plug. The fault often vanishes after a restart and returns under vibration or heat.

causes.label: Loose or poorly crimped terminal in a Circuit A line
Harness rubbing or flexing at a point that moves with the powertrain
Moisture or contamination in the resolver plug

symptoms: Warning lamp that appears and disappears between trips
Brief loss of electric drive or a short jerk
Fault often gone after a restart

P0C55.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit A
P0C55.description: P0C55 is the general circuit code for the first pickup winding (Circuit A) of the resolver on the second traction motor. It applies when the motor B controller recognises a fault on that winding but cannot assign it to a low or high level. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, which runs two motors in the Volt, ELR and the two-mode trucks, files motor B winding faults under P0C57 and P0C58 instead. Compared with P0A45, which reports the motor B angle signal as a whole, P0C55 narrows the search to one winding and its two wires. CARB requires such circuit faults to be detected separately from out-of-range faults. The result is usually a warning lamp and the loss of motor B for drive or charging.

causes.label: Open wire or loose terminal in the motor B Circuit A lines
Damaged or corroded motor B resolver connector
Defective first pickup winding in the motor B resolver

symptoms: Check engine lamp with hybrid system warning
Motor B unavailable, reduced propulsion
Engine may run more often because the second motor is offline

P0C56.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit A Range/Performance
P0C56.description: P0C56 flags a plausibility problem on Circuit A of the motor B resolver: the winding is connected and its level sits inside the electrical window, yet the signal it carries does not fit, for instance because it wanders or no longer matches the second winding. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The closest published case is the motor A version P0C51, which Bentley traces to connector pin fit and contamination on its 2025 Continental hybrids. Possible reasons on motor B are the same kind of contact issue, a resolver with weakened output or interference on poorly shielded lines. P0C57 to P0C59 cover hard low, high and sporadic faults, and P0A46 judges the overall motor B angle signal.

causes.label: Poor pin fit or contamination at the motor B resolver connector
Damaged shield or twisted pair letting interference onto Circuit A
Motor B resolver winding with weakened output

symptoms: Hybrid warning and check engine lamp
Motor B torque limited or switched off
Occasional shudder when motor B takes load

P0C57.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit A Low
P0C57.description: P0C57 means the reference level on Circuit A of the motor B resolver, the S1/S3 winding in GM wiring, has sunk below its limit. GM checks it exactly like the motor A line: under 0.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt and the 2012 two-mode trucks, under 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt, with Type A on the early cars and Type B from 2016. In the field it rarely stands alone. GM preliminary information PIC5856A to F for 2011-13 Volt and 2014-16 ELR groups P0C57 with P0C58 and P0C62: if wiring checks and normal diagnosis find nothing, the motor B position sensor is replaced and the drive motor generator control module is brought to its latest calibration. A genuine harness fault to ground still has to be excluded before any parts are ordered.

causes.label: Faulty motor B position sensor (resolver stator) on Volt and ELR (GM PIC5856)
Circuit A line of motor B shorted to ground in the harness
Drive motor generator control module not on the latest calibration

symptoms: Service engine soon lamp, current or in history
Often stored together with P0C58 and P0C62
Reduced propulsion

P0C58.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit A High
P0C58.description: P0C58 sets when the S1/S3 winding circuit of the motor B resolver shows a reference level above its window, as from an open lead drifting up or a short to voltage. GM limits are 4.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt, 4.9 V on the 2019 Volt and 3.0 V on the 2012 two-mode trucks, with the fast high-side timing of 20 out of 30 samples on early cars. This is one of the most frequent resolver codes on the first-generation Volt. GM's first note PIC5856 from 2013 already paired P0C58 with P0C62, the S2/S4 high code, on 2011-13 Volts: if wiring is fine, a new motor B position sensor goes in, a part ordered through GM's technical assistance center, and update the module calibration.

causes.label: Faulty motor B position sensor on 2011-13 Volt and 2014-16 ELR (GM PIC5856)
Open S1 or S3 line or spread terminal at the resolver connector
Motor control module running an older calibration

symptoms: Check engine lamp, frequently together with P0C62
Reduced propulsion power
Fault may only be in history memory

P0C59.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit A Intermittent/Erratic
P0C59.description: P0C59 reports that Circuit A of the motor B resolver drops out or jumps for moments only, without a fault that persists as low, high or implausible. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Where a dual-motor system uses it, the cause is nearly always mechanical: a terminal that loses grip under vibration, a cable section that flexes with the transmission, or water creeping into a plug. The GM truck note PIP4607A shows how a single poorly crimped terminal at the transmission pass-through connector can upset resolver signals of motor B. Since short glitches on a position signal disturb torque control, the controller may still cut motor B briefly. P0C57 and P0C58 are the steady faults on the same winding.

causes.label: Poorly crimped or loose terminal in the motor B Circuit A path
Wire breaking inside its insulation where the harness flexes
Water ingress at the resolver or pass-through connector

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Short loss of motor B assistance or a jerk
Intermittent start problems on some hybrids

P0C5A.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit B
P0C5A.description: P0C5A is the base circuit code for Circuit B, the second pickup winding of the motor A resolver; GM calls it the S2/S4 winding, set 90 degrees from the S1/S3 winding of Circuit A. The code is meant for a fault on that winding which the controller cannot class as a low or high level. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM checks the S2/S4 line only through P0C5C and P0C5D. If P0C5A appears on its own, the problem is limited to the second winding and its two wires; if P0C50 is stored too, a shared part such as the connector or the excitation side is more likely. P0A3F, by contrast, covers a lost angle signal without naming a winding. Expect a warning and possibly no electric drive.

causes.label: Open wire or loose terminal in the S2/S4 (Circuit B) lines
Damaged or corroded resolver connector
Defective second pickup winding in the resolver stator

symptoms: Check engine lamp with drive system warning
Electric drive limited or unavailable
Vehicle may refuse to enter ready mode

P0C5B.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit B Range/Performance
P0C5B.description: P0C5B is set when the second resolver winding of motor A (Circuit B) stays within its electrical limits yet carries a signal that does not make sense next to the first winding. Bentley added it in revision 3 of bulletin 2080242 for the Continental GT, GTC and Flying Spur hybrids: P0C5B00 now appears alongside P0C5100 and P0A4000, which shows that both windings lose plausibility at once when the shared connection is poor. The repair path is the same, measured value logs, inspection of the 8-pin and 32-pin plugs for pin drag and corrosion, replacement of a 90-degree connector after approval, then basic settings. No threshold is published. P0C5C to P0C5E are the low, high and sporadic Circuit B faults.

causes.label: Insufficient terminal grip at the sensor or power electronics connector
Faulty 90-degree connector on affected Bentley hybrids (TPI 2080242/3)
Corrosion, oil or moisture in the resolver plugs

symptoms: Drive system fault shown in the cluster
Electric drive mode not available
Usually stored together with P0C51 and P0A40

P0C5C.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit B Low
P0C5C.description: P0C5C tells that the reference level on the S2/S4 winding of the motor A resolver, Circuit B, has fallen below its floor. GM uses 0.5 V on the 2011 Volt, 2012 two-mode trucks, 2013 eAssist and the 2016 Volt and ELR, 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt; the low side needs a longer confirmation than the high side, for example 0.525 s within 0.8375 s on the 2016 Volt. On the single-motor eAssist it is a two-trip Type B code. Bentley lists P0C5C00 first in its Bentayga Hybrid note 2066714: damaged 12 V transmission wiring, often with P0C5200 and a temperature sensor code P0A2D00, so a harness worn through on one spot can pull down both windings and other motor sensors at once.

causes.label: Transmission harness chafed or pinched, grounding an S2/S4 line (Bentley TPI 2066714)
Moisture or corrosion in the resolver connector
Shorted S2/S4 winding in the resolver stator

symptoms: Engine warning light, often with P0C52 and a motor temperature code
Electric drive limited or switched off
On mild hybrids loss of start-stop and assist

P0C5D.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit B High
P0C5D.description: P0C5D means the S2/S4 winding circuit of the motor A resolver, Circuit B, reads a reference level above its ceiling. This hints at an open wire whose input floats toward the supply, or contact with a voltage-carrying conductor. GM applies 4.5 V on most of its hybrids, 4.9 V on the 2019 Volt and a much lower 3.0 V on the 2012 two-mode Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Sierra and Silverado. On the 2013 eAssist cars, 20 failed samples out of 30 at 10.4 ms set a two-trip Type B fault; the 2011 Volt uses the same count as a one-trip Type A. When P0C5D appears with P0C53, the shared plug or the resolver itself is more likely than a single wire. No bulletin names this code.

causes.label: Open S2 or S4 wire or backed-out terminal
S2/S4 line touching a voltage-carrying conductor
Broken S2/S4 winding in the resolver stator
Faulty resolver input stage in the motor control module

symptoms: Check engine lamp after one or two trips depending on the vehicle
Electric assist or drive unavailable
Auto stop disabled on mild hybrids

P0C5E.title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit B Intermittent/Erratic
P0C5E.description: P0C5E captures brief interruptions or spikes on Circuit B, the second winding of the motor A resolver, that clear again before a firm low, high or plausibility fault can be confirmed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM leaves such events to the debounce of P0C5C and P0C5D, which on its eAssist cars tolerates short outages and only reports a repeating pattern. Where P0C5E is used, the search starts at the mechanical joints of the S2/S4 path: crimp quality, terminal grip, a cable clip that lets the harness rub on the transmission. Checking resistance while flexing the harness tends to reveal it. P0C54 is the same fault on Circuit A; both together point to the common connector.

causes.label: Loose or weak terminal in the S2/S4 path
Harness rubbing on the transmission because of a missing or broken clip
Moisture entering the resolver plug

symptoms: Warning light appearing only now and then
Momentary drop of electric torque
No fault found on a stationary check

P0C5F.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit B
P0C5F.description: P0C5F is the umbrella circuit code for Circuit B of the motor B resolver, which GM wires as the S2/S4 winding of the second traction motor. It fits a fault on that winding that the controller notices but cannot assign to a low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; on GM's dual-motor hybrids the same winding is covered by P0C61 and P0C62 only. Together, P0C55 and P0C5F let a technician see whether one or both windings of motor B are affected: one alone points to that winding's wires, both together to the shared plug, the excitation or the motor control module. P0A45 reports the overall motor B angle signal. Expect a warning lamp and the loss of motor B.

causes.label: Open wire or loose terminal in the motor B S2/S4 lines
Damaged motor B resolver or pass-through connector
Defective second pickup winding in the motor B resolver

symptoms: Hybrid warning and check engine lamp
Motor B shut off, lower propulsion
Possible no-start on hybrids that crank with motor B

P0C60.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit B Range/Performance
P0C60.description: P0C60 indicates that the second winding of the motor B resolver (Circuit B) is electrically intact but delivers values the controller rejects as unrealistic, for example an amplitude that no longer agrees with the first winding or an angle that jumps against the measured speed. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The idea behind it is the separate rationality test that CARB demands for input sensors, apart from circuit and range checks. Practical suspects are contact resistance at the plug, a resolver stator that has moved or been damaged, and stray coupling from the high-voltage phase cables onto a poorly shielded line. P0C61 to P0C63 cover low, high and sporadic Circuit B faults, P0A46 the combined signal.

causes.label: Raised contact resistance at the motor B resolver connector
Motor B resolver stator shifted or damaged
Interference from the high-voltage phase cables through a damaged shield

symptoms: Hybrid system warning with check engine lamp
Motor B output limited
Vibration or noise when motor B is under load

P0C61.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit B Low
P0C61.description: P0C61 reports a reference level below the lower limit on the S2/S4 winding circuit of the motor B resolver. GM uses 0.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt and the 2012 two-mode trucks, 0.10 V on the 2019 Volt, and needs the low reading for 50 of 80 samples on early cars, 0.25 s within 0.375 s on the 2019 model. A documented field case comes from the 2008 Tahoe and Yukon Hybrid: GM's PIP4607A describes no-crank or intermittent start complaints with P0A45, P0C61, P0A46 and P1B04, traced to a badly crimped pin 20 in the 24-way transmission pass-through connector X176; vehicles built before VIN 8R217000 receive a new internal transmission harness. P0C62 is the high side.

causes.label: Poor crimp at the transmission pass-through connector (GM PIP4607A, 2008 Tahoe/Yukon Hybrid)
S2/S4 line of motor B shorted to ground
Shorted S2/S4 winding in the motor B resolver

symptoms: Engine does not crank or cranks only intermittently
Check engine lamp with several resolver codes of motor B
Reduced propulsion

P0C62.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit B High
P0C62.description: P0C62 means the reference level on the S2/S4 winding circuit of the motor B resolver climbs above its upper limit. GM triggers it at 4.5 V on the 2011 and 2016 Volt and ELR, 4.9 V on the 2019 Volt and 3.0 V on the 2012 two-mode trucks; on the 2016 Volt the level must stay high for 0.2125 s within 0.3125 s, rated Type B over two trips. P0C62 shows up in every GM note of the PIC5856 series, from the 2013 original to version F of 2019, for 2011-13 Volt and 2014-16 ELR, usually paired with P0C58 and sometimes P0C57. Because both windings of the same resolver report high at once, GM's remedy after clean wiring checks is a new motor B position sensor plus the latest module calibration.

causes.label: Faulty motor B position sensor on 2011-13 Volt and 2014-16 ELR (GM PIC5856)
Open S2 or S4 wire or terminal backed out of the connector
Drive motor generator control module without the latest calibration

symptoms: Service engine soon lamp, often with P0C58
Reduced propulsion power
Code may return after clearing until the sensor is replaced

P0C63.title: Drive Motor B Position Sensor Circuit B Intermittent/Erratic
P0C63.description: P0C63 is reserved for short-lived dropouts or erratic jumps on Circuit B, the second winding of the motor B resolver, that do not settle into a steady fault. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The best public illustration comes from GM's 2008 Tahoe and Yukon Hybrid: a weak crimp at the transmission pass-through connector produced intermittent starting with motor B resolver codes, though GM files them under P0C61 and the general P0A45 and P0A46 rather than an intermittent code. That case shows where to look first, crimp joints, pass-through connectors and harness sections near moving parts. Wiggle tests under live data help catch it. P0C59 is the same fault type on Circuit A of motor B.

causes.label: Weak crimp or loose terminal in the motor B S2/S4 path, including pass-through connectors
Intermittent wire break near moving powertrain parts
Moisture or corrosion causing unstable contact

symptoms: Intermittent warning lamp
Occasional start problems or short loss of motor B
Fault not present during a workshop check

P0C64.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit A
P0C64.description: P0C64 is the catch-all entry for the first pickup circuit of the generator resolver, the sensor that reports rotor angle so the inverter can energise the generator phases at the right moment. It is used when the controller judges that circuit faulty without sorting the fault into low, high, implausible or sporadic. No manufacturer documents P0C64 publicly. Mitsubishi shows how such faults get split on the 2023 Outlander PHEV: the sine winding, which it treats as circuit A, has its own low and high codes (P0C66, P0C67), and a failed internal status goes to P0A4B. CARB asks for an approved generator monitoring plan and for circuit and range checks on hybrid inputs. Expect a hybrid system warning and, depending on the design, reduced power or no charging by the engine.

causes.label: Open, chafed or shorted lead in the first resolver pickup winding circuit
Corroded or loose resolver connector between generator and inverter
Damaged pickup winding inside the generator resolver stator
Fault in the generator control electronics of the inverter or power drive unit

symptoms: Hybrid system or malfunction indicator lamp on
Engine runs but the high-voltage battery is no longer charged by the generator
Reduced power or hybrid functions disabled

P0C65.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit A Range/Performance
P0C65.description: P0C65 flags circuit A of the generator resolver as electrically present but not believable. The trace stays between the hard low and high limits, yet its amplitude, centre voltage or relation to the second winding no longer fits the rotor angle the controller expects, for example after the sensor stator has shifted or when the phase cables couple noise into it. No manufacturer documents P0C65 publicly. Mitsubishi runs an analogous window test on the 2023 Outlander PHEV: a sine or cosine level outside 2.1 to 2.9 V for 0.28 s counts as a plausibility fault, but it is filed under P0A4C for the whole sensor. P0C66 and P0C67 cover hard low and high readings on the same circuit. Typical consequences are a hybrid warning and limited use of the generator.

causes.label: Resolver stator loose or shifted, for instance after work on the generator or transaxle
Interference from the phase cables because of a misrouted or damaged resolver harness
Partially damaged winding that weakens the circuit A signal
Generator control software that misjudges a sound signal

symptoms: Hybrid system warning light
Generator use restricted, less charging while driving
Occasional roughness when the engine starts or stops in hybrid mode

P0C66.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit A Low
P0C66.description: P0C66 means the signal of circuit A of the generator resolver has dropped below its lower limit. Mitsubishi uses it on the 2023 Outlander PHEV for the sine winding: the generator control unit, supplied with at least 8 V, watches the line continuously and sets the code when the sine voltage stays at or below 2.000 V for 0.21 s. A short to ground on a sine lead or a damaged winding are the classic causes; a Bosch patent shows that the averaged potential of the coil lines reveals whether a lead touches ground or supply. Mitsubishi first checks for radiator fan codes and tests the resolver circuit, and replaces the power drive unit, or later the generator, only if the code comes back. P0C67 is the high counterpart, P0C6B the same test on the cosine side.

causes.label: Sine lead of the resolver shorted to ground or to the housing
Shorted or damaged sine winding in the generator resolver
Faulty input stage in the power drive unit (generator control unit)
Damaged or contaminated resolver connector pins

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning shortly after switching on
Generator out of service, no charging by the engine
Reduced driving power

P0C67.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit A High
P0C67.description: With P0C67 the controller sees circuit A of the generator resolver stuck above its upper limit. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV Mitsubishi assigns it to the sine winding and trips it once that voltage stays at or above 4.900 V for 0.21 s; the check runs continuously while the generator control unit has 8 V or more. Note the uneven window, since the lower limit is 2.0 V. A lead shorted to a supply potential is the textbook cause, and depending on the input stage an open line can also float high. The Bosch patent on resolver short detection separates both short types by the averaged line potential. Mitsubishi's repair path matches P0C66 and ends with a new power drive unit or generator. P0C6C is the matching cosine code.

causes.label: Sine lead of the resolver shorted to a supply or excitation potential
Open sine lead that floats high at the input stage
Faulty resolver input in the power drive unit
Insulation fault between windings inside the resolver

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Engine-driven charging stops, battery charge falls faster
Power limitation or hybrid functions switched off

P0C68.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit A Intermittent/Erratic
P0C68.description: P0C68 is stored when circuit A of the generator resolver drops out or jumps for short moments and then looks normal again, so neither the low nor the high limit is held long enough to set P0C66 or P0C67. Vibration at a connector, a chafed lead or contacts that loosen with heat are the usual suspects. No manufacturer documents P0C68 publicly. GM gives a practical example for this kind of weakness: on the 2011-12 Volt it replaced the original 2x4 resolver plug of motor A, a part GM lists as the generator position sensor stator, with a sealed 1x6 plug because the signal suffered under vibration, and warns that a misplaced harness lets the phase cables disturb the signal (PIC6136A). Such faults often appear only on rough roads or when hot.

causes.label: Resolver connector with poor contact that opens under vibration
Harness rubbing through intermittently in the transaxle or generator area
Bursts of interference from nearby phase cables due to harness routing
Contact or winding joint that fails only at high temperature

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief jolts or interruptions in generator operation
Fault appears mainly on bad roads or after long drives

P0C69.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit B
P0C69.description: P0C69 is the general fault entry for the second pickup winding of the generator resolver. A resolver needs both windings, set 90 degrees apart, to give an unambiguous rotor angle; with only one, the inverter can no longer place the current in the generator phases correctly. The code applies when circuit B is judged faulty but not classified further. No manufacturer documents P0C69 publicly. At Mitsubishi on the 2023 Outlander PHEV circuit B corresponds to the cosine winding, and that design reports it only through the low and high codes P0C6B and P0C6C. CARB's hybrid rules require the generator to be monitored under an approved plan and circuit faults of input components to be detected. P0C64 is the same entry for circuit A.

causes.label: Open or damaged lead in the second resolver pickup winding circuit
Bent, corroded or pushed-back pins at the resolver connector
Faulty second pickup winding in the resolver stator
Internal fault in the generator control electronics

symptoms: Hybrid warning or malfunction indicator lamp
Generator switched off, battery is no longer recharged by the engine
Limited driving power

P0C6A.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit B Range/Performance
P0C6A.description: P0C6A concerns circuit B of the generator resolver, the cosine side at Mitsubishi: its signal stays inside the electrical limits but does not agree with what the controller expects. Because sine and cosine together describe one angle, a cosine trace with the wrong amplitude or a drifting centre shows up as a mismatch against circuit A, even though no line is shorted. Possible reasons are a loose or twisted sensor stator, a winding with partial damage, or noise picked up from nearby phase leads. No manufacturer documents P0C6A publicly; Mitsubishi's comparable window check on the 2023 Outlander PHEV (2.1 to 2.9 V, 0.28 s) is stored as P0A4C. Hard low or high readings on this circuit belong to P0C6B and P0C6C; the circuit A version is P0C65.

causes.label: Loose or twisted resolver stator changing the cosine amplitude
Partially shorted cosine winding with weakened output
Noise from phase leads due to damaged shielding or poor routing
High contact resistance in the circuit B connector

symptoms: Hybrid warning lamp
Generator used only partly or not at all
Unusual noise or vibration from the transaxle under load

P0C6B.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit B Low
P0C6B.description: P0C6B tells you that circuit B of the generator resolver, the cosine winding, reads too low. In the 2023 Outlander PHEV, Mitsubishi stores it if the cosine signal is no higher than 2.000 V throughout 0.21 s; the test never pauses while the generator control unit receives 8 V or more. To confirm a repair, the matching drive cycle only asks for the power supply mode to be switched ON and a wait of five seconds or more. Likely causes are a cosine lead with a short to ground, a pinched harness near the transaxle or a failing winding. If the resolver circuit tests fine and the code returns, Mitsubishi fits a new power drive unit and, once the EV oil cooling has been checked, a new generator. P0C66 is the sine-side twin, P0C6C the high reading on the same line.

causes.label: Cosine lead of the resolver shorted to ground
Pinched or crushed resolver harness near the transaxle
Shorted cosine winding in the generator resolver
Faulty cosine input in the power drive unit

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp right after switching on
No charging of the drive battery by the engine
Reduced performance in hybrid mode

P0C6C.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit B High
P0C6C.description: P0C6C is the high-side fault of circuit B in the generator resolver. On the 2023 Outlander PHEV, where circuit B is the cosine winding, Mitsubishi triggers it when the cosine voltage sits at 4.900 V or above for 0.21 s; the monitor stays active as long as the generator control unit is supplied with 8 V. First rule out a cosine lead that touches a voltage source, followed by connector damage and an internal fault in the power drive unit, which houses the generator control unit. Mitsubishi also has the radiator fan codes dealt with first and, before fitting a new generator, the EV oil cooling inspected. Unlike P0C6D, the voltage here is held out of range rather than leaving it briefly. P0C67 is the same fault on the sine side.

causes.label: Cosine lead shorted to a supply or excitation line
Damaged resolver connector with bridged pins
Internal fault in the power drive unit holding the generator control unit
Open cosine lead that drifts high at the input

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Generator inactive, state of charge drops while driving
Engine may run more often or the car limits power

P0C6D.title: Generator Position Sensor Circuit B Intermittent/Erratic
P0C6D.description: P0C6D records short, irregular disturbances on circuit B of the generator resolver: the signal flickers, loses samples or jumps, but each event is too brief to count as a hard low or high reading (P0C6B, P0C6C). Because the angle is computed from both windings, even short glitches on the second winding can make the inverter lose track of the rotor for a moment, which may be felt as a jolt or a brief break in charging. No manufacturer documents P0C6D publicly. Typical sources are a terminal with reduced contact pressure, a seal that lets moisture in, or a harness that moves against a bracket. GM's 2011-12 Volt shows how much vibration matters for resolver plugs (PIC6136A). Wiggle tests with live data help to localise such faults; P0C68 is the circuit A equivalent.

causes.label: Terminal with reduced contact pressure in the circuit B connector
Moisture entering through a damaged connector seal
Harness moving against a bracket or edge and breaking contact
Interference spikes from phase cables near the resolver lines

symptoms: Intermittent warning lamp
Short jerks or charging interruptions in hybrid mode
Fault hard to reproduce in the workshop

P0C6E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor A/B Correlation
P0C6E.description: P0C6E compares two battery temperature sensors, A and B, with each other rather than judging either one alone. After a long rest the pack should be close to one temperature, so a lasting gap between the two points to a sensor that reads wrongly while staying electrically valid. No manufacturer documents P0C6E publicly; GM and Mitsubishi run the same idea against the pack average and store per-sensor codes instead. GM's eAssist table 13OBDG05C flags sensor 1 (P0A9C) or sensor 2 (P0AC6) beyond 8.55 °C after more than six hours off, Type B; Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV allows 13 °C after one hour of soak. A Subaru patent compares a sensor pair after parking once both cool at a similar rate. P0C6F covers the B/C pair.

causes.label: Thermistor A or B drifted while staying inside its electrical range
Sensor no longer seated against its cell or module
Genuine temperature difference from uneven cooling or a weak cell group
Battery management software with an over-sensitive comparison

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Reduced charge and discharge power
Battery fan or cooling running more than usual

P0C6F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor B/C Correlation
P0C6F.description: P0C6F sets when battery temperature sensors B and C disagree by more than the calibrated margin. Sensor B also takes part in the A/B check (P0C6E), so the pattern of stored codes helps: if P0C6E and P0C6F appear together, B is the shared suspect, while P0C6F alone points more towards C. No manufacturer documents P0C6F publicly. A Toyota patent describes a second way to catch such faults while the pack is working: if the spread between sensors is large during charging or discharging and one output barely moves, that sensor is treated as frozen. GM files the physical fault per sensor; on the eAssist, sensor 3 is P0ACB with 8.55 °C after six hours off. A real local hot spot inside a module can also open the gap.

causes.label: Sensor C reading off, especially when P0C6F is stored alone
Sensor B reading off, likely when P0C6E is stored as well
Sensor output stuck at one value while the pack temperature changes
Real local heating in a module, for example from a cell with high resistance

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning
Power or charging rate limited
Displayed battery temperatures differ noticeably in live data

P0C70.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor C/D Correlation
P0C70.description: P0C70 is the correlation check between battery temperature sensors C and D. The controller expects both to settle at nearly the same value once the pack has rested, and it stores the code when their difference stays too large. No manufacturer documents P0C70 publicly. Where GM and Mitsubishi publish this monitor, they compare each sensor with the pack average and name the single sensor; GM's sensor 4 code P0AE9 is the D counterpart. Before replacing parts it is worth knowing that GM cured false sets of these Volt sensor codes, shown with a battery-too-cold message, by reprogramming the module (18-NA-342). Genuine faults are a drifting thermistor, a sensor that lost contact with its cells, or uneven cooling. The battery controller usually limits power. P0C71 continues with D/E.

causes.label: Thermistor C or D drifted out of agreement with the other
Battery control software that sets the code falsely, for example in cold weather
Sensor C or D detached from its cell group
Uneven cooling across the pack, such as a blocked air duct or coolant channel

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or EV system warning
Message asking to plug in or warm the battery
Reduced electric power and slower charging

P0C71.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor D/E Correlation
P0C71.description: P0C71 checks whether battery temperature sensors D and E agree with each other. Both sit in the same pack, so after a long soak they should report almost the same value; a lasting gap means one of them reads wrong although its circuit looks healthy. No manufacturer documents P0C71 publicly. GM and Mitsubishi run this plausibility test against the pack average instead and log the single sensor: on the eAssist cars (13OBDG05C) GM flags sensor 4 (P0AE9) or sensor 5 (P0BC3) beyond 8.55 °C after more than 21,600 s off, Type B, while the 2022 Outlander PHEV tolerates 13 °C after one hour. P0C70 covers the C/D pair and P0C72 the E/F pair; open or shorted sensors set their own circuit codes.

causes.label: Thermistor D or E drifted while staying inside its electrical range
Sensor no longer pressed against its cell or module
Genuine temperature difference from uneven cooling or a weak cell group
Battery management software with an overly tight comparison

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Reduced battery charge and discharge power
Battery cooling running more often than usual

P0C72.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E/F Correlation
P0C72.description: P0C72 is the agreement test between battery temperature sensors E and F. The controller stores it when the two readings stay apart by more than a calibrated margin after the pack has had time to even out. No manufacturer documents P0C72 publicly; GM names the matching single-sensor plausibility codes P0BC3 (sensor 5) and P0C34 (sensor 6) and compares each with the pack average, Type B. On the Chevrolet Volt GM traced false sensor codes, together with a battery-too-cold message above -25 °C, to module software and cured them by reprogramming (18-NA-342), so a software check comes before any pack work. If the fault is real, a drifting thermistor, a sensor that lost contact with its module or uneven coolant flow are typical. Battery power is then limited. The D/E pair is P0C71.

causes.label: Battery module software that reports sensor faults falsely, fixed by reprogramming
Thermistor E or F drifted without an electrical fault
Sensor detached from its cell group
Uneven coolant or air flow through the pack

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Battery-too-cold or similar message although it is not very cold
Reduced electric power and range

P0C73.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump A Control Performance
P0C73.description: P0C73 reports that coolant pump A of the motor electronics, the loop that cools the inverter and often the drive motor, does not run the way the controller commands. Kia's bulletins for Niro and Carnival hybrids use exactly this name. The 2018 Outlander PHEV sets it when, with at least 30 % pump command for over 2 s, pump speed stays between 100 and 1,000 rpm or exceeds 5,300 rpm for 0.5 s; Mitsubishi lists air in the loop, wrong coolant level or mix and frozen coolant first. Toyota tied P0C73 on the 2014-2016 Highlander Hybrid to water corroding the inverter pump connector, Kia to water entering the pump can, Mercedes (M264) to trapped air. Battery pack pump faults use P0C47-P0C4D. Power is reduced to protect the inverter.

causes.label: Air trapped in the inverter cooling loop, often after coolant service
Water ingress and corrosion at the pump connector or inside the pump housing
Low coolant level, wrong mixture or frozen coolant
Electric pump worn or seized
Control-unit software with faulty judgement logic

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid warning lamp
Coolant warning in the instrument cluster
Reduced electric drive power at high load

P0C74.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Performance
P0C74.description: P0C74 is the performance check for coolant pump B of the motor electronics, found on vehicles with a second electric pump in the power electronics cooling. The controller compares how the pump should run with how it actually runs and stores the code when the two disagree for longer than calibrated. Stellantis is the only maker found documenting it by code: for 2023-2024 Jeep Renegade and Compass 4xe with the 1.3 L plug-in hybrid, bulletins 08-165-24, 08-193-24 and 08-064-25 cure a lit MIL with P0C74 by flashing new software into the hybrid controller and the power inverter module, with no parts replaced. Where software is current, air in the loop, a worn or blocked pump and wiring faults remain. Pump A uses P0C73, pump C P2BD7.

causes.label: Hybrid control or inverter module software, fixed by an update
Air pocket in the power electronics coolant loop
Pump B worn, blocked or seized
Damaged wiring or corroded connector at pump B

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Reduced electric drive power when the electronics run hot

P0C75.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Discharge Time Too Short
P0C75.description: P0C75 is logged when the high-voltage bus loses its voltage faster than expected after the contactors open. At shutdown the inverter's DC-link capacitor is drained through a discharge resistor or an active discharge circuit, and from capacitance and resistance the controller knows roughly how long that should take. A much quicker drop points to lost capacitance, a lower resistance than designed, a leakage path or a wrong voltage reading. A capacitor diagnostic patent (EP2682769B1) uses the same comparison to detect capacitor ageing. No manufacturer documents P0C75 publicly; GM publishes only the opposite check, P0C76. The driver usually sees a hybrid warning lamp, and depending on the make the next start may be blocked.

causes.label: DC-link capacitor lost capacitance through ageing or damage
Additional load or leakage path on the high-voltage bus
Bus voltage measured incorrectly by the inverter or battery module
Discharge resistor or circuit with too low a resistance

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp
Vehicle may not become ready to drive

P0C76.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Discharge Time Too Long
P0C76.description: P0C76 means the high-voltage bus is still too high a set time after the contactors opened, so the inverter capacitor was not drained as intended. GM publishes thresholds: the 2011 Volt flags more than 200 V after 3.5 s (Special Type C, no MIL), the 2013 eAssist cars more than 65 V after 6.5 s and the 2019 tables more than 200 V after 3.5 s, both Type A after two failed runs. Bulletins name welded contactors on the 2019 Volt (software update, N192226060), a high-voltage cable that had worked loose on the inverter terminal of the 2017 Pacifica Hybrid (08-107-17) and, on GM two-mode trucks, jump-starting with the key on (PIT4585E). A failed discharge circuit is the classic part fault. Treat the bus as live until measured.

causes.label: Active discharge circuit or discharge resistor in the inverter failed
Main contactor welded closed so the battery keeps feeding the bus
Loose high-voltage cable or terminal at the inverter
Low 12 V supply during shutdown or module software

symptoms: Hybrid warning lamp or service high voltage message
Vehicle may not start or become ready
Loss of propulsion

P0C77.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Precharge Time Too Short
P0C77.description: P0C77 is stored when the inverter side reaches battery voltage too quickly during precharge. Before the main contactor closes, the controller charges the inverter capacitor through a precharge resistor and watches the ratio of bus to battery voltage. GM's 2011 Volt sets the code if that ratio passes 95 % within 50 ms of precharge start, Type A; the 2013 eAssist uses 75 ms, Type B, and both require the bus to be below 40 V beforehand. A rise that fast suggests a bypassed or shorted resistor, a main contactor that is welded or closes early, or far less capacitance on the bus than expected. Chrysler lists P0C77 for the 2017 Pacifica Hybrid together with a high-voltage cable that had worked loose on the inverter terminal (08-107-17). Propulsion may be unavailable.

causes.label: Main contactor welded or closing before precharge ends
Precharge resistor bypassed or shorted
Loose high-voltage cable leaving the inverter capacitor partly disconnected
Faulty bus or battery voltage measurement

symptoms: Malfunction indicator or hybrid warning lamp
Vehicle does not become ready or loses propulsion

P0C78.title: Hybrid/EV Battery System Precharge Time Too Long
P0C78.description: P0C78 means precharge took too long: the inverter side did not come up to battery voltage within the allowed time. GM's 2011 Volt allows 700 ms to reach 95 % (Type A), the 2013 eAssist 1,000 ms or more than 5 A for over 100 ms (Type B), and the 2019 tables demand 95-105 % at 0.700 s, Type A. The 2018 Outlander PHEV flags a gap of 12 V or more between battery and inverter after 1 s. Typical causes are an open precharge resistor or fuse, a high-voltage load pulling the bus down, and software. Bulletins cover a blown fuse in the service disconnect (Bolt EV, 18-NA-225), a failed coolant heater (Spark EV, 16-NA-072) and battery-module software at Chrysler and Volvo. The vehicle then normally will not become ready.

causes.label: Precharge resistor, precharge contactor or high-voltage fuse open
Faulty high-voltage consumer such as a coolant heater loading the bus
Battery module software, fixed by an update
Loose high-voltage cable or bus bar

symptoms: Vehicle does not become ready to drive
Malfunction indicator lamp and drive system message
Loss of propulsion

P0C79.title: Drive Motor A Inverter Voltage Too High
P0C79.description: P0C79 reports that the DC voltage at the inverter of drive motor A rose above its protection limit. Overvoltage can come from regenerative energy the battery cannot absorb, from a contactor opening under load or a loose high-voltage connection, and it can also be a false reading. In the 2018 Outlander PHEV a hardware comparator in the front motor control unit trips at 370 V; one event with the IGBTs active, or 0.5 s with them shut down, sets the code; after ruling out other voltage codes, the manual checks the torque of the battery cable at the power drive unit. Subaru revised its diagnosis for the 2014-2015 Crosstrek Hybrid (16-114-18), and Audi traces intermittent P0C7900 on the Q4 e-tron to software. Drive motor B uses P0C7A, the generator P0C7B.

causes.label: Battery cable at the inverter loose or not at specified torque
Inverter or its voltage detection faulty
Voltage spike from regeneration or a contactor opening under load
Motor control software, fixed by an update

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lamp, electrical system fault message
Drive system will not activate or shuts down until restarted
Reduced drive power

P0C7A.title: Drive Motor B Inverter Voltage Too High
P0C7A.description: P0C7A is the overvoltage code for the inverter of drive motor B, which on many all-wheel-drive hybrids is the rear motor. Mitsubishi documents it for the Outlander PHEV: in the 2018 model the rear motor control unit has a hardware high-voltage switch that closes at 420 V, a higher limit than the 370 V of the front unit, and the code sets after a single trip with the power stage active or after 0.5 s with it switched off. The manual blames the high-voltage circuit or the rear control unit and starts with the rear battery cable connections; the 2023 model keeps the code under a rear-motor overvoltage name. Regeneration spikes, contactor events and sensing errors are the usual suspects. Expect a warning lamp and reduced drive power.

causes.label: Rear battery cable connection loose at the rear motor control unit
Rear motor control unit or its voltage detection faulty
Voltage spike from regeneration or a contactor event

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Reduced drive power, rear axle drive may be unavailable

P0C7B.title: Generator Inverter Voltage Too High
P0C7B.description: P0C7B sets when the inverter of the generator, the motor-generator the engine drives to make electricity, sees DC voltage above its limit. Mitsubishi is the only maker found documenting the code by number: in the 2018 Outlander PHEV the generator control unit trips a hardware high-voltage switch at 370 V, and one occurrence with the power stage running, or 0.5 s with it switched off, is enough. The manual suspects the high-voltage wiring as a whole or the generator control unit, and first asks to rule out other voltage codes and to check the tightening torque of the front battery cable at the power drive unit. Overvoltage while generating may also follow a contactor opening under load or false sensing. Expect a warning lamp and limited hybrid operation.

causes.label: Front battery cable at the power drive unit not at specified torque
Generator control unit or its voltage detection faulty
Voltage spike when a contactor opens while the generator charges

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Engine-driven charging or hybrid drive restricted

P0C7C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor G Circuit
P0C7C.description: P0C7C is the umbrella circuit code for battery temperature sensor G, used when the controller sees an electrical fault in that input without sorting it into low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents P0C7C publicly. GM numbers sensor G as sensor 7 of the nine thermistors in the Volt pack (bulletin 18-NA-342), yet its hybrid tables only carry the narrower codes P0C7D to P0C80; Mitsubishi likewise splits sensor G into rationality, short and open. CARB section (e)(15.3.1) asks for continuous checks of range and circuit continuity on every such input. Without a trustworthy reading the battery controller has to assume the worst for that cell group and trims charge and discharge power. The thermistor lives inside the high-voltage pack, so testing needs HV safety procedures.

causes.label: Corroded or loose connector between sensor G and the sensing board
Thermistor G failed electrically
Faulty input stage on the cell monitoring board or battery module

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning lamp, check-engine lamp on many models
Reduced electric power and slower charging
Battery cooling or heating running without obvious need

P0C7D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor G Circuit Range/Performance
P0C7D.description: P0C7D flags sensor G when its value is electrically valid but does not fit the rest of the pack. GM's 2012 Volt table (12OBDG01A) compares it with the average of the other sensors once propulsion has been off for more than 21,600 s and fails it beyond 25.3 °C in 50 of 67 samples, Type B with two trips; bulletin 18-NA-342 calls it sensor 7 performance. Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV of 2018 files it as rationality of sensor [06]: after at least 3,600 s soak, with the pack between −30 and 60 °C, a 13 °C gap from the 50-sensor average held for 0.32 s sets it, checked once per drive. Shorts and opens have their own codes P0C7E and P0C7F. Usual causes are a drifting or detached thermistor; GM also fixed false sets on the Volt with new module software.

causes.label: Thermistor G drifted while staying inside its electrical range
Sensor G no longer seated against its cell group
Battery module software setting the code falsely (GM Volt, 18-NA-342)
Real temperature difference from a weak cell or blocked cooling channel

symptoms: Check-engine or hybrid warning lamp after a long parking period
Reduced battery power, sometimes a battery-too-cold message

P0C7E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor G Circuit Low
P0C7E.description: P0C7E means the sensor G voltage has fallen below its valid range. The thermistor has a negative temperature coefficient and a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground looks like an extremely hot cell group; low describes the signal, not the temperature. GM's 2019 table for hybrid powertrain control module 2 (19OBDG02) fails it when the converted reading exceeds 160 °C in 8 of 10 samples taken every 100 ms, Type B, two trips; bulletin 18-NA-342 files it under sensor 7 as a low-voltage fault on the Volt. Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV of 2022 sets it as a sensor [06] short when the voltage stays under 0.12 V, above 125 °C, for 2 s. The open-circuit opposite is P0C7F; a pack that really runs hot reports P0A7E. Expect power limits and hard-working battery cooling.

causes.label: Sensor G signal line chafed through and shorted to ground
Thermistor G shorted internally, often after moisture entry
Input stage of the cell monitoring board pulled low

symptoms: Warning lamp with sharply reduced electric power
Battery cooling fan or chiller running constantly
Engine runs more often on plug-in hybrids

P0C7F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor G Circuit High
P0C7F.description: With P0C7F the sensor G input reads above its valid voltage range. Because the pull-up raises the line when the thermistor is disconnected, an open circuit, broken wire or unplugged connector shows up as an implausibly cold cell group. GM's 2016 Cadillac ELR table (16OBDG01) sets it below −40 °C for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, two trips, and the 2019 table 19OBDG02 below −69 °C in 8 of 10 samples, Type B. Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV of 2018 calls it a sensor [06] open once the voltage exceeds 3.97 V, colder than −62 °C, for 2 s. On the Volt, GM bulletin 18-NA-342 links these sensor 7 high-voltage sets to a Battery Too Cold message above −25 °C and cures false ones with new software. Its short-circuit partner is P0C7E.

causes.label: Open circuit or unplugged connector at sensor G
Thermistor G open internally
Module software setting it falsely in mild cold (GM Volt, 18-NA-342)

symptoms: Battery-too-cold or plug-in-to-warm message although it is not very cold
Reduced electric power or no electric drive
Battery heater switched on without need

P0C80.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor G Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0C80.description: P0C80 catches a sensor G signal that jumps around instead of following the slow thermal drift of a large battery. GM spells out the logic in its hybrid tables 18OBDG02 and 19OBDG02: every 100 ms the module sums the absolute changes of the reading across a 10-sample window, a total above 10 fails that window, and 4 failed windows out of 5 set the code as Type B, two trips, provided system voltage exceeds 10.2 V and the battery interface module is communicating. Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV has no erratic code for this sensor. The value stays inside its valid range, which separates P0C80 from P0C7E and P0C7F; a loose terminal or a cracked conductor is the usual reason. When several sensors on one board jump together, suspect the board or its supply.

causes.label: Loose or fretting terminal in the sensor G connector
Conductor cracked inside the insulation, breaking under vibration
Cell monitoring board with unstable reference or ground

symptoms: Warning lamp that may come and go between trips
Jumping sensor G value in live data
Occasional power reduction

P0C81.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor H Circuit
P0C81.description: P0C81 reports an electrical fault on the input of battery temperature sensor H that the controller does not narrow down further. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In GM's Volt pack sensor H is sensor 8 (bulletin 18-NA-342), and both the 2016 Cadillac ELR table (16OBDG01) and the later Volt tables list only the specific H codes P0C82 to P0C85. Regulators still expect the input to be watched: CARB section (e)(15.3.1) requires continuous monitoring of value range and circuit continuity for such sensors. If the controller cannot trust H it treats the affected cell group as at risk and limits battery power until the fault clears. A generic circuit code calls for a full check of the wiring and connector from the thermistor to the sensing board, inside the HV pack.

causes.label: Poor contact at the sensor H connector
Thermistor H defective
Damaged measuring channel on the sensing board

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Limited acceleration in electric mode
Charging slower than usual

P0C82.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor H Circuit Range/Performance
P0C82.description: P0C82 is the plausibility test for sensor H: its circuit is fine, but the temperature it reports strays too far from what the rest of the pack says. On the 2016 Cadillac ELR (16OBDG01) GM fails it when the reading differs from the average of the other module groups by more than 20 °C in 50 of 67 samples, Type B; the 2019 table 19OBDG02 allows 25 °C, sampled every 25 ms and only while no low, high or communication fault is active. Mitsubishi files it under sensor [07] in the Outlander PHEV and checks once per drive after an hour of soak against a 13 °C limit. GM bulletin 18-NA-342 names it sensor 8 performance and treats false sets on the Volt with reprogramming. A sensor that came loose from its cells or slowly drifted is the typical real cause.

causes.label: Thermistor H reading off while still electrically valid
Sensor H lifted off its module, measuring air instead of cells
Outdated battery module software (GM Volt, 18-NA-342)
Genuine local temperature difference from poor coolant flow

symptoms: Check-engine or hybrid lamp, often after the car has stood for a while
Battery power limited

P0C83.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor H Circuit Low
P0C83.description: P0C83 stands for a sensor H voltage under its permitted range, which with an NTC thermistor reads as heat: a short to ground or a shorted element makes the cell group seem far too hot. GM's 2016 Cadillac ELR table (16OBDG01) fails it above 87.5 °C, an ADC count below 680, for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, two trips; the Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 files it as the low-voltage fault of sensor 8. Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV of 2018 reports a short of sensor [07] once the voltage sits below 0.12 V, beyond 125 °C, for 2 s, and points to the battery module or its cell monitoring unit. P0C84 is the matching high-voltage fault, P0C82 the plausibility test. Because the controller must assume a hot spot, it cuts power and may run the battery cooling hard.

causes.label: Sensor H signal shorted to ground or to the pack housing
Shorted thermistor H
Fault in the cell monitoring unit that reads sensor H

symptoms: Hybrid warning lamp and strong power reduction
Live data shows sensor H far hotter than its neighbours
Battery cooling running at full effort

P0C84.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor H Circuit High
P0C84.description: P0C84 is set when the sensor H line sits too high in voltage, which the controller converts into an impossible cold reading. The pull-up drives an interrupted circuit upward, so an open wire, a pushed-out pin or a broken thermistor are the classic triggers. In GM's 2012 Volt table (12OBDG01A) the limit is below −40 °C, an ADC count above 4000, held for 1.4 s within a 2 s window; the 2019 table 19OBDG02 uses −69 °C in 8 of 10 samples, Type B. Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV of 2022 sees an open of sensor [07] above 3.97 V, below −62 °C, for 2 s. A cold-weather complaint with a Battery Too Cold message on the Volt may be software, per bulletin 18-NA-342. The short-to-ground counterpart is P0C83.

causes.label: Broken wire or backed-out pin in the sensor H circuit
Thermistor H open
False set by battery module software (GM Volt, 18-NA-342)

symptoms: Battery-too-cold message in mild weather
Electric drive limited or unavailable

P0C85.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0C85.description: P0C85 points to a sensor H reading that flickers. A battery pack warms and cools slowly, so fast swings in one channel suggest an electrical contact problem rather than real heat. GM's 2018 hybrid table 18OBDG02 adds up how much the value moves within a 10-sample window at 100 ms per sample; once that sum passes 10 in 4 of 5 evaluations, the module logs P0C85, Type B over two trips, as long as the supply exceeds 10.2 V and the battery interface module is talking. The 2019 table 19OBDG02 keeps the same rule. GM's OBDG01 tables of 2011 to 2016 (first-generation Volt, ELR) and Mitsubishi list no such code for sensor H. A wiggle test on the harness while watching live data usually finds the fault; low or high voltage faults are P0C83 and P0C84 instead.

causes.label: Intermittent contact at the sensor H terminal
Partly broken sensor H wire inside the pack harness
Noisy measuring channel on the sensing board

symptoms: Intermittent warning lamp
Sensor H value jumping in live data

P0C86.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor F/G Correlation
P0C86.description: P0C86 compares the neighbouring battery temperature sensors F and G with each other. After the pack has rested, both should settle to nearly the same value; a persistent gap means at least one reads wrong although neither circuit is open or shorted. No manufacturer documents P0C86 publicly. GM and Mitsubishi test plausibility against the pack average instead and store the single sensor: GM's 2019 table 19OBDG02 uses a 25 °C margin for P0C34 (sensor 6) and P0C7D (sensor 7), Mitsubishi's 2018 Outlander PHEV 13 °C after 3,600 s soak. CARB lets manufacturers define the rationality checks for such inputs. If a real gap shows, uneven cooling between the two module groups deserves a look. The E/F pair is P0C72, G/H is P0C87.

causes.label: Thermistor F or G drifted without an electrical fault
Sensor F or G no longer in contact with its module
Real temperature difference between the two module groups
Battery management calibration with an overly narrow window

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Somewhat reduced battery power
Sensors F and G far apart in live data after a cold soak

P0C87.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor G/H Correlation
P0C87.description: P0C87 checks that battery temperature sensors G and H tell a consistent story. The controller would set it when, after enough rest for the pack to equalise, the two values remain apart by more than a calibrated margin. No manufacturer documents this pair code publicly. In the Volt, GM numbers G and H as sensors 7 and 8 and, in its 2012 table 12OBDG01A, compares each one with the average of the others after more than 21,600 s off, failing it beyond 25.3 °C as P0C7D or P0C82, Type B. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV logs sensors [06] and [07] the same way against a 13 °C limit. A pair code cannot say which of the two is wrong, so live data after a cold soak decides. The neighbouring pair code is P0C86 (F/G).

causes.label: Thermistor G or H drifted while staying in range
Sensor G or H detached from its cell group
Real temperature gap from a weak cell group or blocked cooling
Battery module software needing an update

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Reduced charge and discharge power

P0C88.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor I Circuit
P0C88.description: P0C88 is the general circuit code for battery temperature sensor I, chosen when the fault is electrical but not classified as low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents P0C88 publicly. In GM's Volt pack sensor I is the ninth and last thermistor (bulletin 18-NA-342); the 2012 Volt table 12OBDG01A and GM's later tables cover it only through the specific codes P0C89 to P0C8C. Packs with more sensors, such as Mitsubishi's Outlander PHEV with 50, carry the letter as channel [08]. CARB section (e)(15.3.1) requires continuous range and continuity checks on such inputs. With channel I unreliable, the battery controller falls back to cautious power limits. Older code lists show this number as reserved, so some scan tools may not name it.

causes.label: Connector fault on the sensor I circuit
Thermistor I failed
Defective input channel in the battery sensing electronics

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning lamp
Reduced electric power
Generic scan tools may show the code without a description

P0C89.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor I Circuit Range/Performance
P0C89.description: P0C89 says sensor I delivers an electrically valid but implausible temperature. GM checks it against the average of the remaining sensors: the 2019 table 19OBDG02 fails it beyond 25 °C in 50 of 67 samples, Type B, two trips, and suspends the test while a low, high or communication fault is present; the 2016 Cadillac ELR table (16OBDG01) uses 20 °C. Bulletin 18-NA-342 calls it sensor 9 performance on the Volt and lists it among the codes cured by reprogramming the hybrid powertrain control module 2. Mitsubishi's 2018 Outlander PHEV treats it as rationality of channel [08], one check per drive after an hour parked, with a 13 °C limit held for 0.32 s. If a software update does not help, a misplaced or drifting thermistor is the likely cause.

causes.label: Module software setting the code falsely, fixed by reprogramming (GM Volt)
Thermistor I drifted within its electrical range
Sensor I displaced from its measuring point
Real local heating at the cell group of sensor I

symptoms: Check-engine or hybrid lamp, often after a long rest
Battery power reduced

P0C8A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor I Circuit Low
P0C8A.description: P0C8A records a sensor I voltage below the valid band. As the element is an NTC thermistor fed through a pull-up, a low voltage translates into a cell group that seems dangerously hot, typically caused by a short to ground. GM's 2012 Volt table (12OBDG01A) trips above 87.5 °C, an ADC count under 680, for 1.4 s within 2 s, two trips; the 2019 table 19OBDG02 instead fails above 160 °C in 8 of 10 samples, Type B. Bulletin 18-NA-342 assigns it to sensor 9 as the low-voltage fault. Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV records a short of channel [08] under 0.12 V, above 125 °C, after 2 s and names the battery module or cell monitoring unit as the part to replace. P0C8B covers the open circuit, P0A7E a pack that really overheats.

causes.label: Sensor I signal shorted to ground
Thermistor I shorted, for example after coolant or moisture entry
Cell monitoring unit input for sensor I faulty

symptoms: Warning lamp with reduced power
Sensor I shown extremely hot in live data
Battery cooling running continuously
